title: A Green Method to Extract Rutin from Sophora Japonica L.
author: Le, Nguyen, et al.
materials: Flower buds powder of S. japonica (sieve 0.5–1.0 mm)
Rutin trihydrate (≥94 %, HPLC, Sigma-Aldrich Co., Missouri, US)
Choline chloride (99 %, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Co., Massachusetts, US)
Ethylene glycol (Xilong Scientific Co., Ltd., Guangdong, China)

steps.title: Prepare ChCl‑Eth DES
steps.instruction: Synthesize the choline chloride‑ethylene glycol deep eutectic solvent (DES) and store it.

substeps.instruction: Transfer both reagents to a 500 mL conical flask.
Stir the mixture at 80 °C for 6 h with a heated magnetic stirrer until a homogeneous fluid is obtained.
Allow the DES to cool to room temperature.
Store the cooled DES in a desiccator.

steps.title: Make 10 % water extraction solvent
steps.instruction: Prepare the DES‑based extraction solvent containing 10 % (w/w) water.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 90 g of the prepared ChCl‑Eth DES.
Mix thoroughly until a uniform solution is obtained.

steps.title: Extract rutin from plant material
steps.instruction: Perform the DES‑based extraction of rutin from Sophora japonica.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 500 mg of dried S. japonica material.
Add 8.5 mL of the 10 % water DES solvent (liquid‑solid ratio 17 mL g⁻¹).
Heat the mixture to 60 °C and maintain for 60 min.
Transfer the mixture to centrifuge tubes (if not already in them).
Centrifuge at 4000 rpm for 10 min using an Electronic Centrifuge 80‑2.

steps.title: Dilute and filter extract
steps.instruction: Prepare the extract for HPLC analysis by dilution and filtration.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the collected supernatant 10‑fold with methanol.
Filter the diluted solution through a 0.45 μm PTFE filter (Whatman plc., Buckinghamshire, United Kingdom).

steps.title: Quantify rutin by HPLC
steps.instruction: Analyze the filtered sample using HPLC under the established rutin assay conditions.
